description: Liwaza Foundation is the team for Liwaza students in grades 8 and 9. On 14–15 November 2026 we will build a simple game or app that lets younger students run a Moon or Mars outpost. Players will have to balance life support, radiation shielding, power, and food, and see how each choice helps the mission succeed or fail. Join this team only if you are in the Liwaza Foundation group.
summary: Our group project is an interactive scratch simulation about the critical decisions made before  and during a space mission, and their realistic effects on the spacecraft and the astronauts. At the beginning of the game(when the player is still on earth),He makes decisions on how to pack food and whether if he needs to pack emergency resources or not. Once the player is on the moon he faces challenges like: the energy has a deficiency, food is inaccessible and how to manage the rest based on his decisions. Our game is important because, its is fun and awakens children's curiosity, while making them think about the consequences of those choices and teaches them the risk of a lunar mission.
details:
Lunar Survival Mission is an interactive decision-making game built on Scratch. The player acts as Mission Control for a lunar expedition and makes critical choices across four phases:

1. Pre-Launch on Earth: Choosing between centralized or distributed food storage, and deciding whether to pack an emergency kit (which adds payload mass and reduces initial energy by 20 kWh).

2. Day 15 (Lunar Night Crisis): Surviving the 14-day lunar night (-130°C, no solar power) by choosing either to conserve energy in low-power sleep mode or to attempt an unrealistic trip to Mercury (which drains fuel due to high Delta-v requirements).

3. Food Compartment Lockout: Managing a 5-day food lockout using distributed storage or the emergency kit to protect crew health.

4. Day 24 (Return to Earth): Managing remaining battery reserves (kWh) for Trans-Earth Injection.

Tools & Creativity:

We developed this project using Scratch (block-based visual programming) with custom variables tracking real mission units (Energy in kWh starting at 240 kWh, and Crew Health at 100%). Our project is creative because it turns complex spaceflight trade-offs—such as the rocket equation, lunar night survival, and Delta-v limits—into a fun, story-driven game that sparks children's and students' curiosity about space exploration.
